# gron

Make JSON greppable!

gron transforms JSON into discrete assignments to make it easier to `grep` for what you want and see the absolute 'path' to it.
It eases the exploration of APIs that return large blobs of JSON but have terrible documentation.

## Example

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author"
json[0].commit.author = {};
json[0].commit.author.date = "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z";
json[0].commit.author.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json[0].commit.author.name = "Tom Hudson";
```

gron can work backwards too, enabling you to turn your filtered data back into JSON:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "commit": {
      "author": {
        "date": "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z",
        "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
        "name": "Tom Hudson"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

## Usage

Get JSON from a file:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json 
json = {};
json.contact = {};
json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
json.github = "https://github.com/tomnomnom/";
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[1] = "cheese";
json.likes[2] = "meat";
json.name = "Tom";
```

From a URL:

```
▶ gron http://headers.jsontest.com/
json = {};
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "gron/0.1";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "6917a823919477919dbc1523584ba25d/11970839830843610056";
```

Or from `stdin`:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron
json = {};
json.Accept = "*/*";
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "curl/7.43.0";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147";
```

Grep for something and easily see the path to it:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep twitter
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
```

gron makes diffing JSON easy too:

```
▶ diff <(gron two.json) <(gron two-b.json)
3c3
< json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
---
> json.contact.email = "contact@tomnomnom.com";
```

The output of `gron` is valid JavaScript:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json > tmp.js
▶ echo "console.log(json);" >> tmp.js
▶ nodejs tmp.js
{ contact: { email: 'mail@tomnomnom.com', twitter: '@TomNomNom' },
  github: 'https://github.com/tomnomnom/',
  likes: [ 'code', 'cheese', 'meat' ],
  name: 'Tom' }
```

It's also possible to obtain the `gron` output as JSON stream via the `--json` switch:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron --json
[[],{}]
[["Accept"],"*/*"]
[["Host"],"headers.jsontest.com"]
[["User-Agent"],"curl/7.43.0"]
[["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"],"c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147"]
```

## ungronning

gron can also turn its output back into JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | gron -u
{
  "contact": {
    "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
    "twitter": "@TomNomNom"
  },
  "github": "https://github.com/tomnomnom/",
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ],
  "name": "Tom"
}
```

This means you can use gron with `grep` and other tools to modify JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

Or with JSON stream mode:

```
▶ gron --json testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --json --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

To preserve array keys, arrays are padded with `null` when values are missing:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[2] = "meat";

▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    null,
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

## Command-line Options

```
Transform JSON (from a file, URL, or stdin) into discrete assignments to make it greppable

Usage:
  gron [OPTIONS] [FILE|URL|-]

Options:
  -u, --ungron     Reverse the operation (turn assignments back into JSON)
  -v, --values     Print just the values of provided assignments
  -c, --colorize   Colorize output (default on tty)
  -m, --monochrome Monochrome (don't colorize output)
  -s, --stream     Treat each line of input as a separate JSON object
  -k, --insecure   Disable certificate validation
  -j, --json       Represent gron data as JSON stream
      --no-sort    Don't sort output (faster)
      --version    Print version information

Exit Codes:
  0	OK
  1	Failed to open file
  2	Failed to read input
  3	Failed to form statements
  4	Failed to fetch URL
  5	Failed to parse statements
  6	Failed to encode JSON

Examples:
  gron /tmp/apiresponse.json
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 
  curl -s http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | gron
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | grep company | gron --ungron
```

## Aliases

It's recommended that you alias `ungron` or `norg` (or both!) to `gron --ungron`:

```bash
alias norg="gron --ungron"
alias ungron="gron --ungron"
```

# Advanced Usage Examples

Although gron's primary purpose is API discovery, when combined with other tools like `grep` it can do some interesting things.

## Examples from the GitHub API

Get the last 5 commits from a repository:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=5"
json = [];
json[0] = {};
json[0].author = {};
json[0].author.avatar_url = "https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/58276?v=3";
...
```

import pty, os, subprocess, sys
def run_tty(args, inp=b'{"a":1}\n'):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()

func formStatements(v interface{}, path []pathElement, pathRaw string, sts *[]statement) error {
    switch t := v.(type) {
    case map[string]interface{}:
        *sts = append(*sts, statement{path: path, rawPath: pathRaw, value: "{}"})
        for _, k := range keys(t) {
            el := makeKeyElement(k)
            formStatements(t[k], append(path, el), pathRaw + elRender(el), sts)

    case []interface{}:
        *sts = append(*sts, statement{path: path, rawPath: pathRaw, value: "[]"})
        for i, e := range t {
            el := pathElement{kind: elemIndex, index: i, raw: "[" + Itoa(i) + "]"}
            formStatements(e, append(path, el), pathRaw + elRender(el), sts)
        }
    default:
        val, err := jsonEncode(v)   // the value text
        *sts = append(*sts, statement{path: path, rawPath: pathRaw, value: val})
    }
}

func openInput(arg string, proxy, noproxy string, insecure bool) (io.Reader, int, error) {
	if arg == "" || arg == "-" {

	f, err := os.Open(arg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 1, err
	}

func isURL(s string) bool {
	i := strings.Index(s, "://")
	if i <= 0 { return false }
	switch strings.ToLower(s[:i]) {
	case "http", "https":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func fetchURL(u, proxy, noproxy string, insecure bool) (io.Reader, int, error) {
	// lowercase the scheme
	i := strings.Index(u, "://")
	scheme := strings.ToLower(u[:i])
	u = scheme + u[i:]
	
	tr := &http.Transport{}
	var proxyURL *url.URL
	if proxy != "" {
		proxyURL, _ = url.Parse(proxy)
	}
	np := strings.Split(noproxy, ",")
	tr.Proxy = func(req *http.Request) (*url.URL, error) {
		for _, h := range np {
			if h == req.URL.Host { return nil, nil }
		}
		return proxyURL, nil
	}
	if insecure {
		tr.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}
	}
	client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
	req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", u, nil)
	if err != nil { return nil, 4, err }
	req.Header.Set("User-Agent", "gron/" + version)
	req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
	resp, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil { return nil, 4, err }
	return resp.Body, 0, nil
}

actions.command:
cd /workspace && cat > /tmp/fuzz3.py <<'PYEOF'
import subprocess, random, sys
ORIG='/workspace/executable'; MINE='/tmp/gron-test'
def run(bin, args, inp=None, timeout=15):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run([bin]+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        return (p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return ('', 'TIMEOUT', -1)
def cmp(args, inp=None):
    a=run(ORIG,args,inp); b=run(MINE,args,inp)
    if a!=b:
        print('MISMATCH', args, repr(inp)[:200])
        if a[0]!=b[0]: print('  SO:',repr(a[0])[:400]); print('  SM:',repr(b[0])[:400])
        if a[1]!=b[1]: print('  EO:',repr(a[1])[:400]); print('  EM:',repr(b[1])[:400])
        if a[2]!=b[2]: print('  rc:',a[2],b[2])
        return False
    return True
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 1)
IDENTS=['json','j','x','a','b','foo','_a','$x','true','null','delete','Ã©','æ','A','Z','a1','a01','x2','x10','zz','abc','Ã¼']
QUOTED=['"a b"','"a.b"','""','"a"','"if"','"a\\tb"','"a\\nb"','"a\\"b"','"a\\\\b"','"\\u0041"','"<>&"','"x"','"\\u00e9"','"10"','"0"','"2x"','"a b c"']
VALS=['1','0','-1','1.5','1e10','"s"','""','"a\\tb"','"\\u0041"','"<>&"','"x"','true','false','null','{}','[]','xyz','1 2','{','[','}',';','','{ }','{} x','x{','+1',',1','1;','"unterminated','"a;b"','1;2','1;','{;','[;','[];','{};','1 {}','"x" {}','1; junk','1\t','1 ;','; junk']
SEPS=['','= ',' = ',' =  ','  = ','=\t','\t= ',' =\t',' =\t1']
PRE=['','json','j','.','','x','[0]','["a"]','.a']
TERM=[';',' ;','; ',';\t',';;','; junk','; junk;','']
WS=['',' ','  ','\t',' \t','\t ','   ']
def rand_line():
    pre = random.choice(PRE)
    parts=''
    for _ in range(random.randint(0,3)):
        r=random.random()
        if r<0.4: parts+='.'+random.choice(IDENTS)
        elif r<0.7: parts+='['+random.choice(['0','1','10','01','1a','a','-1','','01'])+']'
        else: parts+=random.choice(QUOTED) if False else '['+random.choice(QUOTED)+']'
    sep=random.choice(SEPS)
    val=random.choice(VALS)
    term=random.choice(TERM)
    lead=random.choice(WS)
    trail=random.choice(WS)
    line = lead+pre+parts+sep+val+term+trail
    return line
bad=0; ok=0
N=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 400
for i in range(N):
    lines=[rand_line() for _ in range(random.randint(1,3))]
    inp='\n'.join(lines)+'\n'
    for args in (['-u'],['-v']):
        if cmp(args, inp): ok+=1
        else: bad+=1
print('ok=%d bad=%d' % (ok,bad))
PYEOF

// isTerminal reports whether w is attached to a terminal device.
func isTerminal(w *os.File) bool {
	fi, err := w.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	return (fi.Mode() & os.ModeCharDevice) != 0
}

// openInput returns a reader for the requested input together with the exit
// code to use if opening it fails.
func openInput(arg string, opts *options) (io.Reader, int, error) {
	if arg == "" || arg == "-" {
		return os.Stdin, exitOK, nil
	}
	if isURL(arg) {
		body, err := fetchURL(arg, opts)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, exitFetchURL, err
		}
		return body, exitOK, nil
	}
	f, err := os.Open(arg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, exitOpenFile, err
	}
	return f, exitOK, nil
}

// isURL reports whether s names an http or https resource.
func isURL(s string) bool {
	i := strings.Index(s, "://")
	if i <= 0 {
		return false
	}
	switch strings.ToLower(s[:i]) {
	case "http", "https":
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// fetchURL performs the HTTP request and returns the response body.
func fetchURL(raw string, opts *options) (io.Reader, error) {
	i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
	target := strings.ToLower(raw[:i]) + raw[i:]

	var proxyURL *url.URL
	if opts.proxy != "" {
		proxyURL, _ = url.Parse(opts.proxy)
	}
	noProxy := strings.Split(opts.noproxy, ",")

	tr := &http.Transport{}
	tr.Proxy = func(req *http.Request) (*url.URL, error) {
		if proxyURL == nil {
			return nil, nil
		}
		for _, h := range noProxy {
			if h == req.URL.Host {
				return nil, nil
			}
		}
		return proxyURL, nil
	}
	if opts.insecure {
		tr.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}
	}
	client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}

	req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", target, nil)
	if err != nil {

package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

type elemKind int

const (
	elemBareKey elemKind = iota
	elemQuotedKey
	elemIndex
)

// pathElement is a single element of a statement's path.
type pathElement struct {
	kind  elemKind
	key   string
	index int
	raw   string // the element exactly as it was written, brackets included
	quote string // for quoted keys: the quoted string without the brackets
}

// statement is a single gron statement such as `json.foo.bar = "baz";`.
type statement struct {
	path   []pathElement
	raw    string      // the path as it was written (used in error messages)
	value  string      // the value as it was written ("" when unknown)
	jtext  string      // the json encoded value (json stream mode)
	hasEq  bool        // whether the statement contained an '=' at all
	jval   interface{} // the decoded value (json stream mode)
	isJSON bool        // whether the statement came from a json stream
}

// String renders the statement the way gron shows it in error messages.
func (s *statement) String() string {
	if !s.hasEq {
		return s.raw
	}
	if s.isJSON {
		return s.raw + " = " + s.jtext + ";"
	}
	return s.raw + " = " + s.value
}

// sortKey returns the string used to order path elements when sorting
// statements.  Bare keys are prefixed with a dot, quoted keys and indices with
// a bracket, which reproduces the ordering of the original binary.
func (e pathElement) sortKey() string {
	switch e.kind {
	case elemBareKey:
		return "." + e.key
	case elemQuotedKey:
		return `["` + strings.Trim(jsonString(e.key), `"`) + `"]`
	default:
		return "[" + strconv.Itoa(e.index) + "]"
	}
}

// byPath orders statements by their path, comparing element by element.
type byPath []*statement

func (a byPath) Len() int      { return len(a) }
func (a byPath) Swap(i, j int) { a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i] }
func (a byPath) Less(i, j int) bool {
	x, y := a[i].path, a[j].path
	n := len(x)
	if len(y) < n {
		n = len(y)
	}
	for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
		if x[k].kind == elemIndex && y[k].kind == elemIndex {
			if x[k].index != y[k].index {
				return x[k].index < y[k].index
			}
			continue
		}
		xs, ys := x[k].sortKey(), y[k].sortKey()
		if xs != ys {
			return xs < ys
		}
	}
	return len(x) < len(y)
}

func scanQuoted(line string, i int) int {
	j := i + 1
	for j < len(line) {
		switch line[j] {
		case '\\':
			j++
			if j < len(line) {
				j++
			}
		case '"':
			return j + 1
		default:
			j++
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// parseStatement parses a single line into a statement.  It returns
// (nil, nil) when the line does not look like a statement at all, and
// (nil, err) when it fails in a way that gron silently ignores.
func parseStatement(line string) (*statement, error) {
	// Leading spaces are only tolerated for statements without a path, i.e.
	// lines that begin with the "=" separator.
	i := 0
	for i < len(line) && line[i] == ' ' {
		i++
	}
	if i >= len(line) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if i > 0 && line[i] != '=' {
		return nil, nil
	}
	var path []pathElement
	haveRoot := false
	if isIdentStartByte(line[i]) {
		j := readIdent(line, i)
		path = append(path, pathElement{kind: elemBareKey, key: line[i:j], raw: line[i:j]})
		i = j
		haveRoot = true
	}

	for i < len(line) {
		c := line[i]
		switch {
		case c == '.':
			i++
			if i < len(line) && isIdentStartByte(line[i]) {
				j := readIdent(line, i)
				path = append(path, pathElement{kind: elemBareKey, key: line[i:j], raw: "." + line[i:j]})
				i = j
				continue
			}
			return badStatement(line, i)
		case c == '[':
			start := i
			i++
			if i >= len(line) {
				return badStatement(line, i)
			}
			if line[i] == '"' {
				j := scanQuoted(line, i)
				if j < 0 {
					return badStatement(line, len(line))
				}
				if j >= len(line) || line[j] != ']' {
					return badStatement(line, j)
				}
				path = append(path, pathElement{
					kind:  elemQuotedKey,
					quote: line[i:j],
					raw:   line[start : j+1],
				})
				i = j + 1
				continue
			}
			if isDigitByte(line[i]) {
				k := i
				for k < len(line) && isDigitByte(line[k]) {
					k++
				}
				if k >= len(line) || line[k] != ']' {
					return badStatement(line, k)
				}
				idx, err := strconv.Atoi(line[i:k])
				if err != nil {
					return badStatement(line, k)
				}
				path = append(path, pathElement{
					kind:  elemIndex,
					index: idx,

// gronStream handles stream mode, where every line is a separate document.
func gronStream(in io.Reader, w *bufio.Writer, opts *options, colourise bool) error {
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1024*1024), 64*1024*1024)
	root := &statement{value: "[]", hasEq: true}
	if opts.json {
		w.WriteString(renderJSONStream(root, colourise) + "\n")
	} else {
		w.WriteString(renderStatement(root, colourise) + "\n")
	}
	for idx := 0; scanner.Scan(); idx++ {
		dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(scanner.Text()))
		dec.UseNumber()
		tree, err := readTree(dec)
		if err != nil {
			return errors.New(err.Error())
		}
		var sts statements
		formStatements(tree, nil, &sts)
		el := pathElement{kind: elemIndex, index: idx, raw: "[" + strconv.Itoa(idx) + "]"}
		prefixed := make(statements, 0, len(sts))
		for _, st := range sts {
			st.path = withRoot(st.path, el)
			st.raw = renderPath(gronPath(st.path), false)
			prefixed = append(prefixed, st)
		}
		prefixed.sortStatements(opts.noSort)
		for _, st := range prefixed {
			if opts.json {
				w.WriteString(renderJSONStream(st, colourise) + "\n")
			} else {
				w.WriteString(renderStatement(st, colourise) + "\n")
			}
		}
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return errors.New(err.Error())
	}
	return w.Flush()
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------- ungron mode

func ungronMode(in io.Reader, opts *options, colourise bool) int {
	var sts statements
	var err error
	if opts.json {
		sts, err = ungronJSONStream(in)
	} else {
		sts, err = ungronStatements(in)
	}
	if err != nil {
		if se, ok := err.(*statementError); ok {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ungronErrorf(se.st, se.err))
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err.Error())
		}
		return exitParse
	}
	if len(sts) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "no statements were parsed")
		return exitParse
	}
	tree, err := buildTree(sts)
	if err != nil {
		if se, ok := err.(*statementError); ok {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, ungronErrorf(se.st, se.err))
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "failed to merge statements: "+err.Error())
		}
		return exitParse
	}
	out, err := encodeTree(tree, colourise)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "failed to encode JSON: "+err.Error())
		return exitEncodeJSON
	}
	fmt.Print(out)
	return exitOK
}

// statementError carries a statement alongside an error so that gron can
// render the statement in the message.
type statementError struct {
	st  *statement
	err error
}

func (e *statementError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("ungron failed for `%s`: %v", e.st.String(), e.err)
}

// ungronErrorf decorates an error with the statement that caused it.
func ungronErrorf(st *statement, err error) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("ungron failed for `%s`: %v", st.String(), err)
}

// valuesMode prints just the values of the statements found in the input.
func valuesMode(in io.Reader) int {
	w := bufio.NewWriter(os.Stdout)
	defer w.Flush()
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1024*1024), 64*1024*1024)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := scanner.Text()

}

actions.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import subprocess
def scan(lo, hi, step=1):
    bare=[]
    chunk=200
    for base in range(lo, hi, chunk):
        cps=[chr(c) for c in range(base, min(base+chunk, hi)) if c >= 0x80]
        if not cps: continue
        inp = '{' + ','.join('"%s":1'%c for c in cps) + '}'
        p = subprocess.run(['./executable'], input=inp+'\n', capture_output=True, text=True)
        out = p.stdout
        for line in out.split('\n')[1:]:
            if line.startswith('json.'):
                # bare: json.<something> = 1;
                key = line[5:].split(' =')[0]
                bare.append(key)
    return set(bare)
b = scan(0x2100, 0x2200)
print('bare in 2100-21ff:', sorted(b, key=ord))
b = scan(0x2180, 0x21ff)
print('bare in 2180-21ff:', sorted(b, key=ord))
PYEOF

func isSpaceByte(c byte) bool {
	switch c {

func isIdentStartByte(c byte) bool {
	return c == '_' || c == '$' || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') ||
		(c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || c >= 0x80
}

func isIdentContByte(c byte) bool {
	return isIdentStartByte(c) || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')

func isDigitByte(c byte) bool {
	return c >= '0' && c <= '9'

// readIdent returns the index just past the identifier starting at i.
func readIdent(line string, i int) int {
	j := i
	for j < len(line) {
		c := line[j]

			if !isIdentContByte(c) {

s=open('jsonutil.go').read()
s=s.replace('''// jsonString returns the JSON encoding of s.  HTML escaping is disabled so
// that <, > and & appear verbatim, as in gron's output.
func jsonString(s string) string {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	if err := enc.Encode(s); err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.TrimSuffix(buf.String(), "\\n")
}''','''const hexDigits = "0123456789ABCDEF"

// jsonString returns the JSON encoding of s.  HTML escaping is disabled so
// that <, > and & appear verbatim, as in gron's output.  DEL (0x7f) is escaped
// exactly the way gron does.
func jsonString(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteByte('"')
	for i := 0; i < len(s); {
		c := s[i]
		if c < utf8.RuneSelf {
			switch {
			case c == '"':
				b.WriteString(`\\"`)
			case c == '\\\\':
				b.WriteString(`\\\\`)
			case c == '\\n':
				b.WriteString(`\\n`)
			case c == '\\r':
				b.WriteString(`\\r`)
			case c == '\\t':
				b.WriteString(`\\t`)
			case c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f:
				b.WriteString("\\\\u00")
				b.WriteByte(hexDigits[c>>4])
				b.WriteByte(hexDigits[c&0xF])
			default:
				b.WriteByte(c)
			}
			i++
			continue
		}
		r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
		switch r {
		case '\\u2028', '\\u2029':
			b.WriteString(strings.Trim(jsonString(string(r)), `"`))
		default:
			b.WriteString(s[i : i+size])
		}
		i += size
	}
	b.WriteByte('"')
	return b.String()
}''')
s=s.replace('''import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
)''','''import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)''')
open('jsonutil.go','w').write(s)
PYEOF

for v in vals:

// encodeTree renders a merged tree as JSON.
func encodeTree(tree interface{}, colourise bool) (string, error) {
	var b strings.Builder
	if colourise {
		if err := writeColourJSON(&b, tree, 0); err != nil { return "", err }
		return b.String() + "\n", nil
	}
	if err := writePlainJSON(&b, tree, 0); err != nil { return "", err }
	return b.String(), nil
}

func writePlainJSON(b *strings.Builder, v interface{}, depth int) error {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case map[string]interface{}:
		if len(t) == 0 { b.WriteString("{}"); return nil }
		keys := sorted
		b.WriteString("{\n")
		for i, k := range keys {
			if i > 0 { b.WriteString(",\n") }
			b.WriteString(indent(depth+1) + jsonString(k) + ": ")
			writePlainJSON(b, t[k], depth+1)
		}
		b.WriteString("\n" + indent(depth) + "}")
	case []interface{}:
		if len(t) == 0 { b.WriteString("[]"); return nil }
		b.WriteString("[\n")
		for i, e := range t {
			if i > 0 { b.WriteString(",\n") }
			b.WriteString(indent(depth+1))
			writePlainJSON(b, e, depth+1)
		}
		b.WriteString("\n" + indent(depth) + "]")
	case json.Number: b.WriteString(t.String())
	case bool: ...
	case nil: b.WriteString("null")
	case string: b.WriteString(jsonString(t))
	case float64: b.WriteString(jsonMarshal(t))
	}
}

package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// reservedWords is the set of words that may not be written as a bare
// (unquoted) JavaScript identifier in gron's output.  The list was determined
// by probing the original binary with a large number of candidate keys.
var reservedWords = map[string]bool{
	"break": true, "case": true, "catch": true, "char": true, "class": true,
	"const": true, "continue": true, "debugger": true, "default": true,
	"delete": true, "do": true, "else": true, "export": true, "extends": true,
	"false": true, "finally": true, "for": true, "function": true, "if": true,
	"import": true, "in": true, "instanceof": true, "new": true, "null": true,
	"return": true, "super": true, "switch": true, "this": true, "throw": true,
	"try": true, "typeof": true, "var": true, "void": true, "while": true,
	"with": true, "true": true, "yield": true,
}

// isBareKey reports whether key can be written as a bare JavaScript identifier.
func isBareKey(key string) bool {
	if key == "" {
		return false
	}
	for i, r := range key {
		if i == 0 {
			if !isIdentStart(r) {
				return false
			}
			continue
		}
		if !isIdentCont(r) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return !reservedWords[key]
}

// isIdentStart reports whether r may begin a bare JavaScript identifier.
// Letter numbers (such as the roman numerals) are accepted as well.
func isIdentStart(r rune) bool {
	return unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Nl) || r == '_' || r == '$'
}

// isIdentCont reports whether r may appear inside a bare identifier.
func isIdentCont(r rune) bool {
	return unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Nl) || unicode.IsDigit(r) ||
		r == '_' || r == '$'
}

const hexDigits = "0123456789ABCDEF"

// jsonString returns the JSON encoding of s.  HTML escaping is disabled so
// that <, > and & appear verbatim, as in gron's output.  DEL (0x7f) is escaped
// exactly the way gron does.
func jsonString(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteByte('"')
	for i := 0; i < len(s); {
		c := s[i]
		if c < utf8.RuneSelf {
			switch {
			case c == '"':
				b.WriteString(`\"`)
			case c == '\\':
				b.WriteString(`\\`)
			case c == '\n':
				b.WriteString(`\n`)
			case c == '\r':
				b.WriteString(`\r`)
			case c == '\t':
				b.WriteString(`\t`)
			case c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f:
				b.WriteString("\\u00")
				b.WriteByte(hexDigits[c>>4])
				b.WriteByte(hexDigits[c&0xF])
			default:
				b.WriteByte(c)
			}
			i++
			continue
		}
		r, size := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(s[i:])
		switch r {
		case '\u2028':
			b.WriteString(`\u2028`)
		case '\u2029':
			b.WriteString(`\u2029`)
		default:
			b.WriteString(s[i : i+size])
		}
		i += size
	}
	b.WriteByte('"')
	return b.String()
}

// encodeValue renders a decoded JSON value the way gron does.  Numbers keep
// exactly the representation they had in the input.
func encodeValue(v interface{}) string {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case nil:
		return "null"
	case bool:
		if t {
			return "true"
		}
		return "false"
	case json.Number:
		return t.String()
	case string:
		return jsonString(t)
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
	if err := enc.Encode(v); err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.TrimSuffix(buf.String(), "\n")
}

// ------------------------------------------------------- json stream ungron

var errInvalidJSONLayout = errors.New("invalid JSON layout")

// ungronJSONStream reads a gron json stream, one statement per line.
func ungronJSONStream(in io.Reader) (statements, error) {
	var sts statements
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
	scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1024*1024), 64*1024*1024)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := scanner.Text()
		var arr []interface{}
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &arr); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if len(arr) != 2 {
			return nil, errInvalidJSONLayout
		}
		val := arr[1]
		switch t := val.(type) {
		case map[string]interface{}:
			if len(t) > 0 {
				return nil, errInvalidJSONLayout
			}
		case []interface{}:
			if len(t) > 0 {
				return nil, errInvalidJSONLayout
			}
		}
		path, err := jsonStreamPath(arr[0])
		if err != nil {
			if _, ok := err.(errJSONPath); ok {
				return nil, &statementError{st: jsonStatement(path, val), err: err}
			}
			return nil, errInvalidJSONLayout
		}
		sts = append(sts, jsonStatement(path, val))
	}
	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, errors.New(err.Error())
	}
	return sts, nil
}

// jsonStatement builds a statement from the parts of a json stream line.
func jsonStatement(path []pathElement, val interface{}) *statement {
	return &statement{
		path:   path,
		raw:    pathTextRoot(path),
		jtext:  encodeValue(val),
		hasEq:  true,
		jval:   val,
		isJSON: true,
	}
}

// jsonStreamPath converts the path array of a json stream statement into path
// elements.
func jsonStreamPath(v interface{}) ([]pathElement, error) {
	arr, ok := v.([]interface{})
	if !ok {
		return nil, errInvalidJSONLayout
	}
	var path []pathElement
	for _, e := range arr {
		switch t := e.(type) {
		case string:
			path = append(path, pathElement{
				kind:  elemQuotedKey,
				key:   t,
				raw:   "[" + jsonString(t) + "]",
				quote: jsonString(t),
			})
		case float64:
			if t != math.Trunc(t) {
				return append(path, pathElement{
					kind:  elemIndex,
					index: int(t),
					raw:   "[" + encodeValue(t) + "]",
				}), errJSONPath(fmt.Sprintf("invalid integer key `%s`", encodeValue(t)))
			}
			path = append(path, pathElement{
				kind:  elemIndex,
				index: int(t),
				raw:   "[" + encodeValue(t) + "]",
			})
		default:
			return path, errInvalidJSONLayout
		}
	}
	return path, nil
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------- output

// renderStatement renders a statement in gron's own format.
func renderStatement(st *statement, colourise bool) string {
	return renderPath(gronPath(st.path), colourise) + " = " + setValue(st.value, colourise) + ";"
}

// renderJSONStream renders a statement as a line of gron's json stream.
func renderJSONStream(st *statement, colourise bool) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colContainer, colReset, "["))
	sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colContainer, colReset, "["))
	for i, e := range st.path {
		if i > 0 {
			sb.WriteString(",")
		}
		if e.kind == elemIndex {
			sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colNumber, colReset, strconv.Itoa(e.index)))
			continue
		}
		sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colString, colReset, jsonString(e.key)))
	}
	sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colContainer, colReset, "]"))
	sb.WriteString(",")
	sb.WriteString(setValue(st.value, colourise))
	sb.WriteString(colour(colourise, colContainer, colReset, "]"))
	return sb.String()
}

// encodeTree renders a merged tree as JSON, optionally with colours.
func encodeTree(tree interface{}, colourise bool) (string, error) {
	var b strings.Builder
	if colourise {
		colourValueJSON(&b, tree)
		b.WriteString("\n")
		return b.String(), nil
	}
	if err := writePlainJSON(&b, tree, 0); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")
	return b.String(), nil
}

func indentJSON(n int) string {
	return strings.Repeat("  ", n)
}

// writePlainJSON writes v as pretty printed JSON, one that escapes DEL exactly
// the way gron does.
func writePlainJSON(b *strings.Builder, v interface{}, depth int) error {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case map[string]interface{}:
		if len(t) == 0 {
			b.WriteString("{}")
			return nil
		}
		keys := make([]string, 0, len(t))
		for k := range t {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		sort.Strings(keys)
		b.WriteString("{\n")
		for i, k := range keys {
			if i > 0 {
				b.WriteString(",\n")
			}
			b.WriteString(indentJSON(depth+1) + jsonString(k) + ": ")
			if err := writePlainJSON(b, t[k], depth+1); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		b.WriteString("\n" + indentJSON(depth) + "}")
		return nil
	case []interface{}:
		if len(t) == 0 {
			b.WriteString("[]")
			return nil
		}
		b.WriteString("[\n")
		for i, e := range t {
			if i > 0 {
				b.WriteString(",\n")
			}
			b.WriteString(indentJSON(depth + 1))
			if err := writePlainJSON(b, e, depth+1); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		b.WriteString("\n" + indentJSON(depth) + "]")
		return nil
	case json.Number:
		b.WriteString(t.String())
		return nil
	case bool:
		if t {
			b.WriteString("true")
			return nil
		}
		b.WriteString("false")
		return nil
	case nil:
		b.WriteString("null")
		return nil
	case string:
		b.WriteString(jsonString(t))
		return nil
	default:
		enc, err := json.Marshal(t)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		b.Write(enc)
		return nil
	}
}

// colourJSON renders a tree with gron's colour scheme on a single line.
func colourJSON(v interface{}) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	colourValueJSON(&sb, v)
	return sb.String()
}

func colourValueJSON(sb *strings.Builder, v interface{}) {
	switch t := v.(type) {
	case map[string]interface{}:
		keys := make([]string, 0, len(t))
		for k := range t {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
		sort.Strings(keys)
		sb.WriteString(colContainer + "{" + colReset)
		for i, k := range keys {
			if i > 0 {
				sb.WriteString(colBold + "," + colBoldReset)
			}
			q := jsonString(k)
			sb.WriteString(colKey + `"` + colKeyReset)
			sb.WriteString(colKey + q[1:len(q)-1] + colKeyReset)
			sb.WriteString(colKey + `"` + colKeyReset)
			sb.WriteString(colBold + ":" + colBoldReset)
			colourValueJSON(sb, t[k])
		}
		sb.WriteString(colContainer + "}" + colReset)
	case []interface{}:
		sb.WriteString(colContainer + "[" + colReset)
		for i, e := range t {
			if i > 0 {
				sb.WriteString(colBold + "," + colBoldReset)
			}
			colourValueJSON(sb, e)
		}
		sb.WriteString(colContainer + "]" + colReset)
	case json.Number:
		sb.WriteString(colNumber + t.String() + colReset)
	case float64:
		b, _ := json.Marshal(t)
		sb.WriteString(colNumber + string(b) + colReset)
	case bool:
		if t {
			sb.WriteString(colBool + "true" + colReset)
			return
		}
		sb.WriteString(colBool + "false" + colReset)
	case nil:
		sb.WriteString(colBool + "null" + colReset)
	case string:
		s := jsonString(t)
		sb.WriteString(colQuote + `"` + colReset)
		sb.WriteString(colString + s[1:len(s)-1] + colReset)
		sb.WriteString(colQuote + `"` + colReset)
	default:
		b, _ := json.Marshal(t)
		sb.WriteString(string(b))
	}
}

// errJSONPath marks an error in the path of a json stream statement.
type errJSONPath string

func (e errJSONPath) Error() string { return string(e) }

The work is complete. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Approach

I reverse-engineered the `gron` binary purely by running it with many different inputs and flags (never decompiling or tracing it), then wrote a from-scratch Go implementation.

## Key behaviours discovered through probing

- **Statement format**: `json.a.b = "x";` with bare vs. quoted keys (`json["a b"]`, `json["a-b"]`) and array indices (`json[0]`), plus a hard-coded list of ~37 reserved words that must be quoted (determined by brute-forcing every 1–6 letter lowercase word and a large curated candidate list).
- **Sorting**: element-by-element comparison of rendered path elements (`.key` / `["key"]` / `[N]`), with array indices compared numerically and string keys lexically.
- **`--no-sort`**: walks the decoded tree in Go map order (so the output is genuinely nondeterministic).
- **`-s` stream mode**: emits a `json = [];` header, then per-line documents prefixed with `[i]`, printing incrementally before erroring.
- **`-j` JSON stream**: `[path,value]` lines; ungron mode validates the shape (`invalid JSON layout`), integer indices (`invalid integer key`), and non-empty container values.
- **`-u` ungron**: an elaborate line parser (spaces-vs-tabs asymmetries, `-` treated specially, `{`/`[`/`"` value scanning, `;` terminator rules) plus a recursive merge that unwraps a single `json` root, and distinct error renderings for `invalid statement`, `statement has no value`, `invalid value`, and `invalid quoted key`.
- **`-v` values**: prints the raw value (unescaped strings, containers skipped, `true/false/null` right-trimmed), silently ignoring parse errors but failing on blank/indented lines.
- **Colours**: exact ANSI sequences, including the compact single-line coloured ungron output, and DEL (0x7f)/U+2028 escaping.
- **HTTP fetching**: `gron/dev` User-Agent, `Accept: application/json`, scheme lowercasing, `-x`/`--noproxy` (exact `Host:port` matching) and `-k`.

## Result

~1600 lines of original Go in `src/`, with `compile.sh` building `./executable` from a clean checkout. Thousands of differential tests and fuzz runs were used to match behaviour; the exit codes, help text, error strings and colour codes were verified byte-for-byte.
